source.note: Battery 5 (6-inch) at Castle Bluff and the Fort Tidball buildings, Long Island (kadiak.org, Joe Stevens).

k_long_is_jun22_18.caption: Aerial view of battery with North Cape off to the top of the picture. This bunker containins a BD-74 telephone switchboard on the lower level and the battery spotting and plotting room. Photo June 22, 1998.
k_long_is_jun22_18.credit: Photo: Joe Stevens, from a helicopter, 22 June 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_long_is_li07.caption: This is the lower level entrance to the bunker. It is located to the left just under the trees in the above photo.

k_long_is_li09.caption: Both of the 6-inch M1903A2 gun barrels are missing. This is gun No. 1 looking toward the battery command post.

k_long_is_li10.caption: The splinter shield of the north gun, No. 2, is upside-down.

k_long_is_296wide.caption: [SCR-296A steel radar tower, Castle Bluff, from the helicopter, 22 June 1998.]
k_long_is_296wide.credit: Photo: Joe Stevens, from a helicopter, 22 June 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_long_is_aug03_04.caption: Several electrical poles are still standing. Ft. Tidball had an extensive overhead electrical distribution system.

k_long_is_aug03_05.caption: Even though this mess hall has collapsed, the sink is in comparatively good condition.

k_long_is_aug03_12.caption: The huts have numbers painted on them to help the Corps of Engineers cleanup contractor tell where they are.

k_long_is_aug03_13.caption: This interior clearly demonstrates the roof framing. The KIMSUL Insulation (by Kimberly Clark) is still hanging in there.
